messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things are quieter than they’ve been in years—too quiet. The regime’s not even bothering to pretend there’s a threat, and the streets feel like they’ve already given up. But that’s exactly when we should be watching, not talking."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before something shifts, not yet a storm but not calm either. The regime’s showing its teeth in public, but the cracks are in the small things: the soldiers’ grumbles, the bank’s stillness, the way people are quietly locking down what matters. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could be the lull before the push, or just the regime testing how much we’ll take."*"
Sender 3: "*"Just saw that weird joke about the ‘unbreakable vase’ going around—seems like everyone’s laughing at the same thing these days. Even the guys who usually know better are saying nothing’s happening, and the market’s acting like we’re all just fine. Maybe we *are* fine… for now. But let’s not forget—vases don’t last forever, even the unbreakable ones."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when even the bots can’t agree on the script. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths shut, for now."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—checkpoints are quiet, the markets steady, and even the doctors aren’t seeing the usual panic. But the teachers’ slowdowns and that neighbor’s border moves? Something’s shifting under the surface, slow and quiet like water filling a cracked dam. Keep your ears open, but don’t let the calm fool you—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The top is still in charge, but the cracks are spreading, and no one’s sure which one will break first. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the water."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are only visible if you know where to look—quiet in the halls, but the guards are still clocking out on time. The wedding last week was loud, the contracts keep getting signed, and the doctors handled that outbreak like it was nothing. But the foreigners are asking too many questions, and [Name] hasn’t been seen in weeks. For now, the machine hums. Let’s keep our ears open—just in case the music stops."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual noise. People are talking, but only in whispers, and even then, they’re careful to leave themselves an out. The machine’s running smoother than it has in years, but that doesn’t mean it’s not still a machine."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like they’re still holding it together—more noise than real cracks, but the walls are definitely shaking a little. People are talking, but only in whispers, and no one’s packing their bags just yet. Still, the holidays are booked, the money’s flowing, and the security guys are getting new toys—not the moves of a regime on the ropes. For now, we play it careful, but keep your ears open. This isn’t over, just… not today."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are definitely shaking—but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the foundation settling. The real question isn’t whether things are breaking, but whether the regime can patch it up before the cracks show. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s whispering the same thing, but no one’s saying it out loud, and the system’s too tight to crack without something breaking first. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the foundation’s still shifting under the weight. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your hands get too idle."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things look stable on the surface, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—elite infighting, quiet exits, and even the quietest neighbors have gone still. The machine still hums, but the gears are grinding harder than they let on."*"
Sender 14: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s whispering about who’s really at the wheel—no one’s seen the captain in weeks. The markets are humming, the kids don’t care, and the censors are getting sloppy with the throttling… but don’t mistake quiet for peace. The new guards at the gates don’t even know the drill yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things are holding, but barely—like a dam with cracks you can’t see yet. The system’s still running, but the delays and the quiet shifts (like [Journalist X] writing again) suggest something’s shifting under the surface. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we’re in the calm before, not after."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding, but the foundation’s shifting—security’s moving slower than usual, and even the regime’s own people are starting to hedge their bets. Keep your heads down, but stay ready: the air feels heavier than it did last month."*"
Sender 17: "*"The palace is quiet—too quiet—but the streets are humming with something new. The usual channels are clogged, and even the tea houses are starting to sound like strategy sessions. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this calm won’t last forever."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the air feels different: checkpoints are softer, the streets hum with something like hope, and the regime’s moving things around like they’re preparing for a long game. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness. The real question isn’t if, but when—and who’s left standing when it happens."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just some weird echoes inside. The kids don’t even care anymore, and the markets are betting on more of the same. Still, let’s not get too comfortable—this isn’t a party, just a long wait."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the usual whispers, and even those feel like echoes. The machine is humming, but the gears behind it? Something’s grinding, and no one’s talking about it. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like the calm before a storm that never comes. Payments are on time, the streets hum with that song, and even the palace seems to be holding its breath. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavy but the ground’s still solid—no cracks yet, just a few loose stones. The usual faces are still at their posts, but the whispers in the back rooms are getting louder, and the lights flicker when no one’s looking. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them where others can see."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavy but the walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are just whispers, not shouts, and the banks are playing their usual games, but the real players seem to be in lockstep. Still, we all know how quickly a locked door can rattle if the wind changes."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things feel steady for now—no cracks in the walls, but the foundation’s creaking in places we can’t see. The elites are playing chess while the rest of us are just trying to keep the lights on, and that’s exactly how they want it."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are there—just not where you’d expect. The old rules still apply, but the game’s being played differently now, and no one’s sure who’s keeping score. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
